title: Modulus of Subgrade Reaction (Plate Load Test)
applicability: k depends on plate size, moisture, loading sequence, and depth of influence (~1.5–2 × plate diameter). Correct to 762 mm (30 in) plate for pavement design: k_30 ≈ k_plate × (d_plate/762). k for rigid pavement design: AASHTO 1993 or MEPDG input.

title: DCP to CBR Correlation (USACE / ASTM D6951)
applicability: Most widely used correlation. Valid for a wide range of soils. Other correlations: CBR = 1/(0.017×DCPI)² (South Africa), log(CBR) = 2.46 - 1.12×log(DCPI) (Australia). Always verify with laboratory CBR for critical applications.
source: ASTM D6951, USACE TL-99-10, Webster et al. (1992)

title: CBR to Resilient Modulus Correlation

M_R.description: Resilient modulus (subgrade stiffness for pavement design)

applicability: AASHTO 1993 design guide correlation. Approximate — actual M_R depends on stress state, moisture, and soil type. For CBR 2–20: reasonable estimate. For design, prefer resilient modulus from triaxial testing (AASHTO T307) or FWD back-calculation.
source: AASHTO Guide for Design of Pavement Structures (1993)

title: Clegg Impact Value to CBR Correlation

CIV.description: Clegg Impact Value (4th drop, standard 4.5 kg hammer)

applicability: Approximate correlation; varies significantly by soil type. Use for screening and relative comparison, not for design. Other correlations exist for specific soil groups.

title: LWD Dynamic Deformation Modulus
equation: E_vd = f × (1 - ν²) × σ₀ × r / d₀

f.description: Shape factor (2 for rigid plate, π/2 for flexible plate)

applicability: Based on Boussinesq elastic half-space solution. E_vd is a dynamic modulus — generally higher than static plate load modulus. Ratio E_vd/E_static varies 1–3 depending on soil type and stress level. Target E_vd values are agency-specific.
source: ASTM E2583, German TP BF-StB Part B 8.3

title: FWD Back-Calculated Subgrade Modulus

d_r.description: Deflection at distance r from load center

r.description: Distance from load center to the deflection sensor used

applicability: Simplified AASHTO method using outer sensor deflection (where pavement layer influence is minimal). Full back-calculation uses all sensor deflections and iterative layer analysis (MODULUS, ELMOD, BAKFAA software). For bare subgrade, simpler Boussinesq-based analysis.

title: Proof Rolling — Deflection Criterion
equation: Pass if δ_rut < δ_max (typically 25 mm / 1 in)

δ_rut.description: Observed rut depth under loaded roller

δ_max.description: Maximum allowable rut depth per specification

applicability: Qualitative and semi-quantitative. Modern intelligent compaction rollers (IC) measure continuous compaction values (CMV, MDP, CCV) that provide quantitative mapping of entire area. FHWA has guidance on IC specifications and acceptance criteria.

title: Plate Load — Bearing Capacity from Load Test
equation: q_ult = P_failure / A_plate   or   q_allow = q_at_δ_allow / FS

q_ult.description: Ultimate bearing capacity from plate load test

P_failure.description: Load at failure (or at defined displacement)

q_allow.description: Allowable bearing pressure at acceptable settlement

applicability: Plate load test directly measures bearing response but only for shallow depth (1.5–2× plate diameter influence zone). For full-scale footing design, must account for size effect: settlement of footing = settlement of plate × (B_footing/B_plate)^n where n ≈ 0.5–1.0.
